title: CLEAN experimentally identifies SAM hydrolase activity in previously uncharacterized proteins
summary: Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign developed CLEAN, a contrastive-learning enzyme-function predictor, and used it to identify the SAM hydrolase activity of the previously uncharacterized protein TTHA0338. In vitro HPLC–MS and enzyme-kinetic experiments also corrected the annotation of MJ1651 and confirmed the multiple activities of SsFIA.
organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Cornell University; Georgia Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: In vitro HPLC–MS and enzyme-kinetic experiments also corrected the annotation of MJ1651 and confirmed the multiple activities of SsFIA.
evidence.unknown: The study validated a small, selected set of proteins, and also showed CLEAN can assign functions to non-enzymes; the demonstrated result is specific to the tested proteins. TTHA0338 is one of multiple results reported by this paper; record describes the previously unknown function rather than treating every model benchmark as a separate discovery.
evidence.ai_role: CLEAN predicted enzyme commission functions from protein sequences; researchers then validated the predicted activity experimentally. It was the model that nominated TTHA0338 as a SAM hydrolase, not an autonomous discovery or validation system.
